question.problem: Let $f$ be a function such that ${f}^{′}(x)=5x-3$ and $f(2)=-1.$ Use the tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at $x=2$ to estimate the value of $f(2.4).$
question.worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at the point $a=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =f(2)+{f}^{′}(2)(x-2).\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that $f(2)=-1,$ and since ${f}^{′}(x)=5x-3,$ then ${f}^{′}(2)=5(2)-3=7.$ So, the tangent line approximation is given by

$$
L(x)=-1+7(x-2).
$$

Now, we can approximate $f(2.4)$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $x=2.4.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2.4) & ≈L(2.4) \\  & =-1+7(2.4-2) \\  & =-1+7(0.4) \\  & =-1+2.8 \\  & =1.8.\end{aligned}
$$
